To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EP-changes in the visual cortex are not a consequence of the motivational state, but are a consequence of the behavioral activity.
EP-changes in the visual system are dependent on the motivational level.
EP-changes in the brain structures of rabbits are not only dependent on the motivational state, but also on the motivational level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how far EPs can be used to characterize different motivational levels.
the question of the significance of EP-changes during a motivational state and their dependence from the behavioral situation of the animal.
the question of the role of the visual system in the regulation of feeding behavior and its relation to the motivational state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EP-configuration in the visual cortex and the sensomotors area is not a reliable parameter for the determination of motivational level in the rabbit.
the motivational state has a significant influence on the neuronal processing of visual information.
the EP-changes during the food expectance are a result of an interaction between nonspecific arousal, motivational specific activation and the actual behavioral state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EP-changes are dependent upon the motivational level, the behavioral situation, and the brain structures.
the EP-configuration depends on a motivational state and that the EP-activity is modulated by motivational specific mechanisms of the activation.
the EP-changes in visual cortex and other brain structures during the pseudoconditioning experiment are a result of the motivational state of the animal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EP-changes are a result of a complex interaction of different mechanisms of neuronal activation.
EP-changes during active food expectance can be explained by a nonspecific and also a specific motivational mechanism.
the changes in the evoked potentials are not only dependent on the motivational state, but also on the specific motivational situation.
